title: GamePreview
responsibility: Run native key-door gameplay and preserve progress while keeping optional AI video disabled by default.

inputs.name: GamePreview.view
inputs.description: Supplies the level data and render dimension used by the canvas, gameplay steps, reset and AI prompt. Its style updates an active AI prompt, and a change to the derived level key or dimension resets the run to initialRun or a fresh spawn run.

inputs.name: GamePreview.initialRun
inputs.description: Optional run snapshot used when the derived view scope initializes and to restore progress at that view's spawn. Defaults to undefined; when absent the component creates createRun(1, view) before calling atSpawn.

inputs.name: GamePreview.projectId
inputs.description: Project identifier forwarded to bridge.gameRender when AI video starts. A null or empty string prevents AI video availability and start.

inputs.name: GamePreview.readonly
inputs.description: When true, disables AI video availability while local gameplay and reset remain interactive. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: GamePreview.onRun
inputs.description: Called with the run after scope initialization, each gameplay step and reset. Its return value is ignored.

inputs.name: GamePreview.bridge
inputs.description: Optional desktop bridge supplying gameRender for AI video sessions; without the bridge or method, AI video is unavailable. Defaults to undefined.

outputs.name: GamePreview
outputs.description: Provides a dimension-selected 2D or 3D canvas, GameControls, and one Live AI video button; its dialog (desktop.component.game-live-ai) holds the AI video model, the price, the start or stop control and the status line. AI video availability requires a ready Decart transport, a truthy projectId, a gameRender bridge method, and readonly=false; sessions pass a 60-second limit and failures appear as an alert.

errors.name: Renderer initialization or run callback error
errors.description: Exceptions from run creation or stepping, canvas drawing or rendering, renderer setup, or onRun are not caught here and can propagate from the lifecycle or interaction that invokes them. Rejections from bridge.gameRender or connectDecart are caught and displayed as alert text instead.
